service: Pharmacogenomic testing of CYP2C9 or VKORC1 alleles to predict warfarin response
vignette: 73-year-old woman with newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation who started warfarin 4 days ago; her cardiologist plans long-term warfarin therapy. She has never had CYP2C9 or VKORC1 genotyping. She has enrolled in a prospective, randomized, controlled trial comparing genotype-guided warfarin dosing with standard dosing in Medicare-aged adults; its outcomes are major and minor hemorrhage, thromboembolism and mortality. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov by its sponsor before the first subject was enrolled, has a written protocol that addresses the Medicare CED standards, is IRB-approved and complies with 45 CFR Part 46, and specifies public release of results within 24 months of the end of data collection. The test is ordered as part of the trial.
rationale_note: Boundary: 4 days of warfarin (fewer than five). Never genotyped; enrolled in a qualifying RCT.
